# Section 10: Educational Policies, Procedures, and Practices

Section 10 addresses admissions, academic, and student policies.

## Standard 10.1 — Academic Policies

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution publishes academic policies including admission, progression, grading, and completion requirements.

### Typical Evidence Types

- College catalog
- Website academic policies
- Student handbook
- Admissions materials

### Suggested Owners

- Registrar
- Admissions Director
- Chief Academic Officer

---

## Standard 10.2 — Public Information

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Current and prospective students have access to accurate information about the institution, its programs, costs, and policies.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Website content audit
- Catalog
- Consumer information
- Cost of attendance information

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Outdated website information
- Inconsistent information across publications
- Missing required consumer disclosures

---

## Standard 10.3 — Archived Policies

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Policies affecting students are archived for historical reference.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Archived catalog system
- Policy archive procedures
- Evidence of accessibility

---

## Standard 10.4 — Academic Governance

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Faculty have primary responsibility for curriculum and academic matters.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Curriculum committee composition
- Faculty governance documentation
- Examples of curriculum approval process

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges submit curriculum changes through the SBCC approval process. Document:

- Local curriculum committee process
- State approval process for new programs
- Combined Course Library requirements
:::

---

## Standard 10.5 — Admissions Policies

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Admissions policies are consistent with institutional mission and published.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Admissions policies
- Application requirements
- Program-specific requirements

---

## Standard 10.6 — Distance Education/Correspondence

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

If offering distance education, appropriate policies exist for delivery, oversight, and student support.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Distance education policies
- Learning management system documentation
- Student verification procedures
- Distance education support services

---

## Standard 10.7 — Policies for Awarding Credit

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Policies exist for awarding academic credit consistently.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Credit hour policy
- Transfer credit policy
- Credit for prior learning policy

---

## Standard 10.8 — Evaluating and Awarding Credit

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Credit evaluation follows established policies consistently.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Transcript evaluation procedures
- Credit acceptance guidelines
- Articulation agreements

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges operate under the Comprehensive Articulation Agreement (CAA) for transfer to UNC System institutions. Document:

- CAA implementation
- Transfer equivalency processes
- Articulation agreements with other institutions
:::

---

## Standard 10.9 — Cooperative Academic Arrangements

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Any cooperative academic arrangements maintain quality and appropriate oversight.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Consortium agreements
- Contractual arrangements
- Oversight documentation

---

## Reflective Prompts

- Are all academic policies easily accessible to students?
- How do we ensure policy consistency across formats (web, catalog, etc.)?
- What processes verify transfer credit evaluation consistency?
